title: Quantities and Unit-Aware Arithmetic
description: CQL Quantities are numbers WITH units — 1 'g' equals 1000 'mg' because comparisons are unit-aware. Write quantity literals, combine them across units, project .value/.unit, and compare calendar durations.
learningObjectives: Multiply a quantity by a scalar

hints.message: Quantity literal syntax: number, space, quoted UCUM unit — 5 'mg'.
1 'g' = 1000 'mg' is TRUE — CQL converts to a common unit before comparing.
180 'cm' < 2 'm' — same conversion logic applies to < and >.
1 'g' + 500 'mg' — the result converts to the most granular unit: 1500 'mg'.
Quantity * number scales the value and keeps the unit: 10 'mg'.
ToString(5 'mg') renders the CQL literal form: 5 'mg' with the unit quoted.
(5 'mg').value projects the numeric value; note it comes back as the Decimal 5.0.
UCUM temperatures: 37 'Cel' > 30 'Cel' — Celsius has its own UCUM code, not 'C'.
Calendar durations compare by conversion: 1 year > 11 months is true.
between works on quantities, unit-aware: 7.5 'mg' between 5 'mg' and 10 'mg'.
